sentence.ja: {月曜日[げつようび]}に日本語[にほんご]のクラスがあります。
sentence.en: I have Japanese class on Mondays.

mnemonic.story: Day names end in yōbi, and getsu is the moon. **Monday** *gets* you every week: the moon is still up when the alarm goes off. Getsu-yōbi: Monday.

sentence.ja: {火曜日[かようび]}に山田[やまだ]さんに会[あ]いました。
sentence.en: I met Yamada-san on Tuesday.

mnemonic.story: Ka is fire. Every **Tuesday** your old *car* coughs and bursts into flames in the driveway, and you toast marshmallows over it. Ka-yōbi: Tuesday.

sentence.ja: {水曜日[すいようび]}は図書館[としょかん]で勉強[べんきょう]します。
sentence.en: On Wednesdays I study at the library.

mnemonic.story: Sui is water. On **Wednesday** you fill the trough and holler the old pig call, "*Sooey!*", and the pigs come splashing. Sui-yōbi: Wednesday.

sentence.ja: {木曜日[もくようび]}は学校[がっこう]へ行[い]きません。
sentence.en: I don't go to school on Thursdays.

mnemonic.story: Moku is wood. On **Thursday** you burn a pile of damp wood and thick *smoke* rolls over the fence; drop the s and you have mok-. Moku-yōbi: Thursday.

sentence.ja: {金曜日[きんようび]}に友達[ともだち]とカフェへ行[い]きます。
sentence.en: I'm going to a cafe with a friend on Friday.

mnemonic.story: Kin is gold. **Friday** is payday, and all your *kin* line up at the door for their share of the gold coins. Kin-yōbi: Friday.

sentence.ja: {土曜日[どようび]}はたいてい十時[じゅうじ]に起[お]きます。
sentence.en: On Saturdays I usually get up at ten.

mnemonic.story: Day names end in yōbi, "day of the week", and do is soil. On **Saturday** a *doe* digs in your garden, hooves black with soil. Do-yōbi: Saturday.

sentence.ja: {日曜日[にちようび]}に山田[やまだ]さんのうちへ行[い]きます。
sentence.en: I'm going to Yamada-san's place on Sunday.

mnemonic.story: Nichi is the sun, so nichi-yōbi is sun-day: **Sunday**, literally. Sunlight pours into a wall *niche* and warms it like a little oven. Nichi-yōbi.

sentence.ja: {週末[しゅうまつ]}はよくカフェへ行[い]きます。
sentence.en: I often go to cafes on weekends.

mnemonic.story: Every **weekend** you drag the *shoe mats* out to the balcony and beat them, thwack, thwack, a week of dust in the air. Shūmatsu: weekend.

sentence.ja: {今日[きょう]}はどこへ行[い]きますか。
sentence.en: Where are you going today?

mnemonic.story: In *Kyoto* a temple bell booms once and the calendar on the gate rips off its page: **today** has begun. Kyō is just the Kyo of Kyoto: today.

sentence.ja: {明日[あした]}は何[なに]をしますか。
sentence.en: What are you doing tomorrow?

mnemonic.story: *A cheetah* sprints so fast it reaches **tomorrow** before you do, and is waiting at your bedroom door when you wake, yawning. Ashita: tomorrow.

sentence.ja: {昨日[きのう]}は何[なに]をしましたか。
sentence.en: What did you do yesterday?

mnemonic.story: Patting every pocket, you remember **yesterday**: you locked the door, and your *key*... *no!* It's still on the kitchen table. Kinō: yesterday.

sentence.ja: {あさって}は友達[ともだち]の誕生日[たんじょうび]です。
sentence.en: The day after tomorrow is my friend's birthday.

mnemonic.story: **The day after tomorrow** you're grilling *a satay* skewer on the balcony, peanut sauce spitting on the coals. Ashita, then asatte: one day further.

sentence.ja: {おととい}、本屋[ほんや]へ行[い]きました。
sentence.en: I went to the bookstore the day before yesterday.

mnemonic.story: **The day before yesterday** you stepped barefoot on a *toy*: "*Oh! Toe!*" It still throbs. Ototoi ends in i, a day; ototoshi ends in toshi, a year.

sentence.ja: {毎日[まいにち]}日本語[にほんご]を勉強[べんきょう]します。
sentence.en: I study Japanese every day.

mnemonic.story: Mai means every and nichi means day: **every day** you set a fresh flower in *my niche* in the hallway wall. Mai-nichi.

sentence.ja: {今週[こんしゅう]}の土曜日[どようび]は何[なに]をしますか。
sentence.en: What are you doing this Saturday?

mnemonic.story: Kon is "this", as in konban, tonight; shū is week: **this week**. On the shoe rack, konshū's pair is missing, because those *shoes* are on your feet. Kon-shū.

sentence.ja: {来週[らいしゅう]}の金曜日[きんようび]に田中[たなか]さんが来[き]ます。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san is coming next Friday.

mnemonic.story: Rai means coming, the one ahead; with shū, week, it's **next week**. You bake a loaf of *rye* bread for next week's picnic. Rai-shū.

sentence.ja: {先週[せんしゅう]}、京都[きょうと]へ行[い]きました。
sentence.en: I went to Kyoto last week.

mnemonic.story: **Last week** a *cent* got stuck in your *shoe*, and you limped on it for seven days before shaking it out. Sen-shū: last week.

sentence.ja: {毎週[まいしゅう]}、母[はは]に電話[でんわ]します。
sentence.en: I call my mother every week.

mnemonic.story: Mai means every, as in mainichi. Shū is the week from shūmatsu and its *shoe* mats. So **every week** you drag those shoe mats outside and beat them again. Mai-shū: every week.

sentence.ja: {今月[こんげつ]}は毎日[まいにち]公園[こうえん]へ行[い]きました。
sentence.en: I've gone to the park every day this month.

mnemonic.story: Kon, this, plus getsu, month: **this month**. Tonight's moon is a thin curl, like the rim of an ice-cream *cone*. Kon-getsu.

sentence.ja: {来月[らいげつ]}、アメリカへ帰[かえ]ります。
sentence.en: I'm going back to America next month.

mnemonic.story: Rai, coming, plus getsu, month: **next month**. Next month's moon will rise over a field of ripe *rye*. Rai-getsu.

sentence.ja: {先月[せんげつ]}はアルバイトがたくさんありました。
sentence.en: I had a lot of shifts at work last month.

mnemonic.story: Sen, previous, as in senshū; getsu, month, the moon of getsu-yōbi: **last month**. Last month's moon hung low and round like a copper *cent*. Sen-getsu.

sentence.ja: {今年[ことし]}は日本[にほん]にいます。
sentence.en: I'm in Japan this year.

mnemonic.story: **This year** your resolution is the *koto*, the long Japanese zither, and by December your fingertips are hard as nails. Koto-shi: this year, a reading of 今年 all its own.

sentence.ja: {来年[らいねん]}、日本[にほん]の大学[だいがく]へ行[い]きます。
sentence.en: Next year I'm going to a Japanese university.

mnemonic.story: Rai, coming, plus nen, year: **next year**. You sow *rye* this autumn and harvest it next year, golden and rustling. Rai-nen.

sentence.ja: {去年[きょねん]}は大学[だいがく]の一年生[いちねんせい]でした。
sentence.en: Last year I was a first-year at university.

mnemonic.story: Nen is year, as in ichi-nensei; kyo means gone. **Last year** is the gone year: you drop its calendar into a *Kyoto* canal and watch it float off. Kyo-nen, with a short kyo.

sentence.ja: さくらさんの{誕生日[たんじょうび]}はいつですか。
sentence.en: When is Sakura-san's birthday?

mnemonic.story: On his **birthday**, *tan Joe* lies on the beach until he is toasted brown, the candles on his cake melting beside him. Tanjō is birth, bi is the day of nichi-yōbi. Tanjō-bi: birthday.

sentence.ja: 明日[あした]は{休[やす]み}です。
sentence.en: Tomorrow is a holiday.

mnemonic.story: The boss asks who wants a **holiday** and you leap onto your desk shouting "*Yes, me!*", papers flying everywhere. Yasumi: holiday, day off; also an absence.

sentence.ja: {朝[あさ]}は何[なに]を食[た]べますか。
sentence.en: What do you eat in the morning?

mnemonic.story: Every **morning** at sunrise *a saw* starts buzzing next door, and sawdust drifts through your window onto the pillow. Asa: morning.

sentence.ja: {今朝[けさ]}は何[なに]も食[た]べませんでした。
sentence.en: I didn't eat anything this morning.

mnemonic.story: **This morning** starts with a breakfast *quesadilla* so hot the cheese strings from your mouth to the plate. Bite off only the front, quesa-: kesa, this morning.

sentence.ja: {夜[よる]}はたいてい家[うち]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。
sentence.en: At night I usually read at home.

mnemonic.story: "*Yo, roo!*" you hiss into the dark, but the pet kangaroo keeps bouncing on your bed, springs twanging all **night** long. Yoru: night.

sentence.ja: {今晩[こんばん]}電話[でんわ]します。
sentence.en: I'll call you tonight.

mnemonic.story: You already say *konbanwa*, "good evening", which is literally "this evening is...". Drop the wa and konban is this evening: **tonight**.

sentence.ja: {毎晩[まいばん]}十一時[じゅういちじ]に寝[ね]ます。
sentence.en: I go to bed at eleven every night.

breakdown.baseEn: to sleep, to go to sleep

mnemonic.story: Mai means every and ban means evening: **every night** you light *my bonfire* in the back yard, same crackle, same smoky sleeves. Mai-ban.

sentence.ja: 明日[あした]は五時[ごじ]に{起[お]きます}。
sentence.en: I'm getting up at five tomorrow.

mnemonic.story: The alarm blares, your feet hit the cold floor, and you **get up**: "*Okey*-dokey, here we go." Oki-ru: to get up.

sentence.ja: ケンさんは十二時[じゅうにじ]ごろ{寝[ね]ます}。
sentence.en: Ken goes to bed around midnight.

breakdown.baseEn: to sleep, to go to sleep

mnemonic.story: A horse **sleeps** standing up in its stall, one last drowsy *neigh* fading into a snore. Ne-ru: to sleep.

sentence.ja: 九時[くじ]に仕事[しごと]を{始[はじ]めます}。
sentence.en: I start work at nine.

mnemonic.story: Every friendship **begins** with *hajime*mashite and a bow on day one. Strip off -mashite, add -ru, and you have the verb for starting anything. Hajime-ru: to begin.

sentence.ja: 昨日[きのう]は友達[ともだち]と{出[で]かけました}。
sentence.en: I went out with friends yesterday.

mnemonic.story: You *deck a cake* with sprinkles, box it, and **go out** the door to the party with frosting smeared on your sleeve. Dekake-ru: to go out.

sentence.ja: 映画[えいが]が{始[はじ]まりました}よ。
sentence.en: The movie has started!

mnemonic.story: *Ha, Jim, a roo!* A kangaroo bounds onto the stage, the drums thump, and the show **begins**. Hajima-ru: (something) begins; hajime-ru is you starting it.

sentence.ja: 試験[しけん]が{終[お]わりました}。
sentence.en: The exam is over.

mnemonic.story: The show flops and **ends** to a sad trombone, *oh, wah-wah*, the last note sliding down as the curtain thuds shut. Owa-ru: (something) ends.

sentence.ja: 昨日[きのう]、学校[がっこう]を{休[やす]みました}。
sentence.en: I was absent from school yesterday.

mnemonic.story: A *sumo* wrestler is asleep across the school doorway. "*Ya*, sumo..." you sigh, and you are **absent** from class all day, napping on his warm belly. Yasum-u: to be absent; also to rest.

sentence.ja: 時間[じかん]がありませんから、{急[いそ]いで}ください。
sentence.en: There's no time, so please hurry.

mnemonic.story: "*Eee, soggy!*" you squeal as the rain soaks through your socks, and you **hurry** home, shoes squelching at every step. Isog-u: to hurry.

sentence.ja: 学校[がっこう]でテニスを{します}。
sentence.en: I play tennis at school.

mnemonic.story: A lawyer slaps papers on your desk: "**Do** it, or we *sue*." Your pen scratches as you sign. Su-ru: to do.

sentence.ja: 今晩[こんばん]、お母[かあ]さんに{電話[でんわ]します}。
sentence.en: I'm going to call my mom tonight.

mnemonic.story: Denwa is telephone, suru is to do: "doing the phone" is **to call**. The phone in your *den* wails *wah, wah* like a baby until you call back. Denwa suru: to call.

sentence.ja: 毎朝[まいあさ]{シャワーを浴[あ]びます}。
sentence.en: I take a shower every morning.

breakdown.baseEn: to bathe in, to take (a shower)

mnemonic.story: Shawā is shower; abiru means to have something pour over you. *A bee* hovers under the spray beside you, soaked and buzzing, as you **take a shower**. Shawā o abi-ru.

sentence.ja: 毎晩[まいばん]、{お風呂[ふろ]に入[はい]ります}。
sentence.en: I take a bath every night.

breakdown.base: お風呂[ふろ]に入[はい]る

mnemonic.story: Japanese doesn't take a bath, it walks into one: ofuro, the *furrow*-fingers bath, ni hairu, enter. You step over the tub's edge like a doorway and sink to your chin. Ofuro ni hairu: **to take a bath**.

sentence.ja: すみません、少[すこ]し{遅[おそ]くなります}。
sentence.en: Sorry, I'll be a little late.

mnemonic.story: "*Oh, soak* five more minutes," you sigh in the warm tub, while the clock keeps ticking and you **become late**. Osoku is late, naru is become. Osoku naru: to be late.

sentence.ja: 朝[あさ]は{いつも}コーヒーを飲[の]みます。
sentence.en: I always drink coffee in the morning.

mnemonic.story: Your cat **always** *eats more*: full bowl, empty bowl, then a hard stare and a paw rattling the dish across the floor. Itsu is when; itsumo is every when. Itsumo: always.

sentence.ja: 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]は{たいてい}うちで食[た]べます。
sentence.en: I usually eat dinner at home.

mnemonic.story: You **usually** order *Thai tea*: the same orange glass, the same rattle of ice, every single time. Taitei: usually.

sentence.ja: {よく}このカフェへ来[き]ます。
sentence.en: I come to this cafe a lot.

mnemonic.story: You crack an egg and **often** find a double *yolk*: two yellow eyes staring up at you from the pan, again. Yoku: often.

sentence.ja: {時々[ときどき]}ハンバーガーを食[た]べます。
sentence.en: I sometimes eat hamburgers.

mnemonic.story: You keep a spare *toe key* in your sock, because **sometimes** the *door key* goes missing; it sits cold against your foot. Toki-doki: sometimes.

sentence.ja: 魚[さかな]は{あまり}食[た]べません。
sentence.en: I don't eat much fish.

mnemonic.story: Do you sail from *a marina*? **Not much**: last time a gull stole your sandwich and you sat on wet rope all afternoon. Amari with a negative: not much.

sentence.ja: お酒[さけ]は{全然[ぜんぜん]}飲[の]みません。
sentence.en: I don't drink alcohol at all.

mnemonic.story: Two *Zen* monks sit perfectly still on either side of you while you fidget and itch: you are **not at all** calm. Zenzen with a negative: not at all.

sentence.ja: {もう}晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べました。
sentence.en: I've already had dinner.

mnemonic.story: You drag the mower out to *mow* the lawn, but it is **already** cut, neat green stripes and the smell of fresh grass. Mō: already.

sentence.ja: 十月[じゅうがつ]ですが、{まだ}寒[さむ]くないです。
sentence.en: It's October, but it isn't cold yet.

mnemonic.story: From the back seat you wail "*Ma! Da!* Are we there?" and the answer is always **not yet**, then another hour of humming tyres. Mada + negative: not yet.

sentence.ja: {すぐ}電話[でんわ]してください。
sentence.en: Please call right away.

mnemonic.story: The race starter drops the flag: "*Sue, go!*" Your friend Sue bolts **right away**, gravel spraying from her heels before anyone else has moved. Sugu: right away.

sentence.ja: 今[いま]忙[いそが]しいですから、{後[あと]で}電話[でんわ]します。
sentence.en: I'm busy right now, so I'll call you later.

mnemonic.story: "*A toad, eh?* I'll move it **later**," you mumble, and the toad on your pillow croaks all evening, cold and damp against your cheek. Ato de: later on.

sentence.ja: 「朝[あさ]、公園[こうえん]へ行[い]きました。」「{それから}？」
sentence.en: "I went to the park this morning." "And then?"

mnemonic.story: Sore is "that" and kara is "from": from that, **and then**. Your road trip goes breakfast, sorekara the *car*, sorekara the beach, sorekara ice cream. Sore-kara.

sentence.ja: さくらさん、{早[はや]い}ですね。
sentence.en: Sakura, you're early!

mnemonic.story: At four a.m. a rooster karate-chops your alarm clock with a "*Hi-yah!*": far too **early**. Haya-i: early.

sentence.ja: このパソコンはとても{遅[おそ]い}です。
sentence.en: This computer is really slow.

mnemonic.story: The last bus crawls up the hill, *oh so* **slow**, and you let out a long "eee" at your watch: late again. Oso-i: slow, late.

sentence.ja: 仕事[しごと]は九時[くじ]{から}です。
sentence.en: Work starts at nine.

mnemonic.story: A flag drops and your *car* roars away **from** the starting line, tires squealing, smoke everywhere. Kara: from. After a sentence, kara means because.

sentence.ja: 仕事[しごと]は五時[ごじ]{まで}です。
sentence.en: Work goes until five.

mnemonic.story: You slog all the way **to** the finish line through knee-deep *mud, eh*, every step a sucking squelch. Made: to, until. Kara and made together: from and to.
